articles.title: India cuts windfall tax on diesel, raises petrol tax from July
articles.titleEn: India cuts windfall tax on diesel, raises petrol tax from July
articles.summary: India has adjusted its windfall taxes on fuel exports, slashing duties on diesel and aviation fuel while increasing the tax on petrol exports. These changes, effective July 1, reflect easing global oil prices and aim to secure domestic supply. Exemptions for exports to neighbouring countries have also been expanded. This move signals a shift in the government's approach to managing fuel revenues amidst fluctuating international markets.
articles.summaryEn: India has adjusted its windfall taxes on fuel exports, slashing duties on diesel and aviation fuel while increasing the tax on petrol exports. These changes, effective July 1, reflect easing global oil prices and aim to secure domestic supply. Exemptions for exports to neighbouring countries have also been expanded. This move signals a shift in the government's approach to managing fuel revenues amidst fluctuating international markets.

articles.title: India Adjusts Windfall Taxes Amid Shifting Global Oil Prices
articles.titleEn: India Adjusts Windfall Taxes Amid Shifting Global Oil Prices
articles.summary: India has modified its windfall taxes on diesel and aviation turbine fuel exports, reducing them as global oil prices decline. Meanwhile, petrol export duties have increased. The changes aim to balance exports with domestic supply needs. The tax adjustments reflect economic forecasts and geopolitical developments impacting oil markets.

articles.title: Will Petrol And Diesel Prices Fall in India Again?
articles.titleEn: Will Petrol And Diesel Prices Fall in India Again?
articles.summary: India’s crude basket has fallen below $70 a barrel, easing the import bill and inflation, but petrol and diesel prices are unlikely to drop immediately as oil marketing companies focus on recovering past losses. Experts say any fuel price cuts may only come from August, possibly timed with upcoming state elections.

articles.title: Auto demand likely to remain strong, easing crude, aluminium, PGM prices to support margins: Kotak
articles.titleEn: Auto demand likely to remain strong, easing crude, aluminium, PGM prices to support margins: Kotak
articles.summary: India's automobile sector is likely to remain on a strong footing in the coming quarters, as demand has remained resilient despite the hike in petrol and diesel prices. In addition, easing commodity costs are expected to provide much-needed relief to automakers' profit margins, according to a report by Kotak Institutional Equities.
